newsitem.title: SWEDEN: INTERVIEW - KLM cargo has Sweden ambition.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - KLM cargo has Sweden ambition.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV's cargo division has high hopes to raise its market share in the Nordic region and has rejigged its freighter operation, a spokesman for the airline said on Wednesday.

"We are today ranked the third carrier volume wise out of Sweden and we have a definite goal to become number two," Michael Steen, regional director of sales for the Nordic Region, told Reuters in an interview.
Steen said the company aimed to increase its market share by lifting its profile.
"(We are aiming to do this) by being a lot closer to the market, by being more visible," he said.

KLM Cargo said it will start at least five flights a week from Sweden's Skavsta airport in Nykoping, located 100 kms southwest of Stockholm, to its European hub at Amsterdam's Schiphol starting from February 17.

"KLM Cargo has decided to move its flown cargo operations from Stockholm Arlanda airport to Nykoping Skavsta airport from February 17," KLM Cargo said in a statement released in Stockholm at the interview.
KLM currently flies a Belfast freighter with a capacity of 30 tonnes five times weekly from Stockholm's Arlanda international airport.

KLM Cargo gave no details about which aircraft it would be using on the Skavsta-Amsterdam route and said the current flights from Arlanda would not necessarily be the same as the schedule from Skavsta.
Steen said the move was partly based on Skavsta's proximity to several major Swedish air cargo shippers.
"The location of Skavska is very good," he said.

"There are a lot of shippers who have their factories in the southern outskirts of Stockholm. You have a lot of Ericsson factories, Astra pharmaceuticals, car manufacturing industries, a lot of other electronics producing companies," Steen said.
He said Arlanda airport would become more of a trucking point for KLM.
"We will feed the cargo delivered here onwards down to Skavsta by truck," Steen said.
KLM also flies a Lockheed Electra with a 15 tonne capacity from southern Swedish city Malmo daily from Tuesday to Sunday.
Cargo from Norway is trucked to the Malmo freighter, while cargo from Finland is trucked both to Stockholm and to Malmo.
Steen, who is also in charge of cargo sales for the St Petersburg region, said cargo from this part of Russia was flown on passenger flights or trucked to Malmo.
KLM's shipments to its Amsterdam hub from the St Petersburg region include airplane parts, heavy machinery and art from the Hermitage museum.
"We are seeing steady growth, both inbound and outbound," Steen said about the Russian region.
